specGaps: SG-1 — THE PLAN'S G5 STEP PUTS A ROUTER IN A PIPELINE THAT SENDS IT NO TRAFFIC (the one real hole, and it makes the literal instruction nearly vacuous). plan:2884-2888 says 'run Task 13.1's scripted e2e twice — once with the router in the loop, once with --no-router', but plan:2918-2921 makes 13.1 model-free: it drives the REAL hooks/handlers/state against a fixture repo 'using the FAKE SDK programmed with realistic canned outputs', so NO provider HTTP is issued by the run at all. With the fake SDK in place the router's only reachable surface is the report's injected metrics thunk (9.5b), which means an unqualified two-arm comparison would compare two runs that differ in one optional HTTP GET and would pass on a router that was never in any loop. RESOLUTION: 12.1-G5 runs THREE legs, all scripted: LEG A is the plan's literal instruction (all five 13.1 scenarios, both arms, normalized digest comparison — rows -terminal-state-identical, -item-dispositions-identical, -commit-set-identical, -report-identical-except-metrics); LEG B supplies the traffic the fake SDK cannot, by reusing the COMMITTED wire-contract vehicle (real `opencode serve` + tests/fixtures/stub-llm-server.ts, wire-contract.test.ts:5-16) and running one identical scripted conversation twice — arm N with opencode's provider baseURL pointing at the stub directly (`http://127.0.0.1:<stub>/v1`, the serve.py:217 shape), arm R with it pointing at a real llama-router whose `upstream` is that same stub (rows -traffic-leg-router-actually-in-path, -status-equivalence-per-request, -schema-tagged-never-rejected, -stream-relay-equivalent, -no-admission-refusal-by-construction); LEG C exercises the fail-soft direction by killing and by corrupting the router (rows -router-killed-midrun-still-identical, -hostile-router-still-identical, -supervisor-restart-observed). REASONING: G5's property is about REQUESTS ('the router never returns a status the direct path would not have returned', plan:90-91), so a G5 test with no requests through the router is a test of nothing; and this build has banked the same failure twice already (C-033: the stub always set a Content-Length, so the streaming path — the one that mattered — was never exercised though every row was green; C-034: a deleted guard failed nothing because only one of two paths was under test). Leg B is built ENTIRELY from committed fixtures, so it adds a vehicle, not an architecture.

SG-2 — WHAT DOES 'ROUTER IN THE LOOP' MEAN TO THE PLUGIN? Nothing in the plugin's own config says a router exists: Config (core/types.ts:135-172) has no router block, and RouterClientConfig (router-client.ts:55-58) is adapter-local with no committed producer. PROPOSED RESOLUTION (ORCHESTRATOR DECISION, and it is 12.1-core's + 10.1's to make — this step must CONSUME it, not invent it): the arm difference reaches the system through exactly TWO seams and no others — (i) opencode's provider `options.baseURL` in the session config serve.py writes (serve.py:217): the router's listen origin under `--router`, the upstream origin under `--no-router`; and (ii) the injected `metrics` thunk 9.5b's handleReport takes (staging/task-9.5b/tools-9.5b.test.ts:176): bound to `fetchMetricsSummary` with a RouterClientConfig derived from the §2.2 file `.data/configs/conductor-router.json` listen block plus §7.2's 2 s probe timeout (plan:2507) when the router is enabled, and left absent/null-returning under `--no-router`. Adding a `router` block to §2.1's Config is NOT proposed (schema change), and probing for a router the session was not told about is NOT proposed (it would make `--no-router` depend on whatever else is listening on the machine). CONSEQUENCE FOR THIS STEP: row -baseurl-only-difference asserts seam (i) is the only textual difference between the two session configs, and row -report-identical-except-metrics asserts seam (ii) is the only difference in the run's own artifacts. If 12.1-core resolves the seams differently, THOSE TWO ROWS change and no other row does.

SG-3 — 12.1-G5 HAS NO COMMIT, YET IT MUST LAND EXECUTABLE CODE. STATE.json's row sets manifest:false and commitMessage null ('no separate commit'), but plan:2885 says 'assert', and an assertion needs a driver in the tree. RESOLUTION: the driver (conductor/tests/e2e-g5.test.ts + its normalizer) and the recorded artifact land in ONE non-manifest commit `conductor-build: 12.1-G5 equivalence`, on the C-007 precedent (CORRECTIONS.md:70-78: non-manifest commits do not match the `^conductor: ` grep and do not disturb verify-acceptance.sh's exactly-once check on the manifest messages). ALTERNATIVE, if the orchestrator prefers to keep Phase 13's commit count clean: run the step before 13.1's commit and let the driver ride inside `conductor: 13.1 e2e scripted`. Either is defensible; what is NOT defensible is landing test code with no commit and no STATE row, so the 12.1-G5 STATE row is filled in (tap, redEvidence, filesTouched, finishedAt) whichever is chosen.

SG-4 — 13.1 MUST EXPOSE ITS SCENARIO DRIVER (a requirement on a task that is NOT_STARTED, recorded now so it is absorbed rather than discovered). To run 'the same e2e' twice under two configurations, 13.1's five scenarios must be callable as a function — approximately `runScenario(scenarioId, {fixtureRoot, config, sdk, metrics, opencodeBaseUrl}) -> {run, items, questions, decisions, reportMd, commits}` — with its top-level `test()` bodies as thin callers. RESOLUTION: state the requirement in 13.1's own spec; if 13.1 lands with everything inline, 12.1-G5 costs a refactor of a committed test file, which is worse than shaping it once. This step does NOT fork 13.1's scenarios into a second copy: two divergent copies of the e2e would make the equivalence claim meaningless the first time one of them was edited.

SG-5 — §4.4's PROVIDER-TRAFFIC FAILOVER IS UNWIRED AND, THROUGH OPENCODE, UNWIREABLE. plan:1689-1691 says the plugin 'fails over to the upstream base URL for the remainder of the session'; plan:2503-2504 names the fan-out engine as the consumer. VERIFIED: resolveBaseUrl/noteRouterFailure have no caller outside router-client.ts and its own test, fanout.ts never mentions the router, and provider traffic's base URL is opencode's, fixed in the session config serve.py writes at :217 and read at session start — the plugin cannot change it mid-session. RESOLUTION: 12.1-G5 asserts ONLY what it can observe (the health/metrics probes are fail-soft; the run's outcome is unchanged when the router dies; the 12.1-core supervisor restarts it) and makes NO claim of provider-traffic failover anywhere in its artifact; row -failover-limit-recorded states the limit in words and hands it to Task 15.1's HONEST-LIMITS. Wiring failover is NOT in scope here — it would be new behaviour in a task whose whole point is that it adds none.

SG-6 — THE ROUTER 404s EVERY NON-/v1 PATH, WHICH IS A LITERAL G5 EXCEPTION IN COMMITTED CODE (router.hpp:85-89 `"/v1/.*"`, :5-8 'everything else is 404'd without touching the upstream'). llama-server itself serves /health, /props, /slots and /completion; through the router those become 404s the direct path would not have returned. RESOLUTION: this step does NOT assert the exception away and does NOT propose widening the proxy (a general reverse proxy is a different component with a different blast radius). It asserts the narrower true statement — that the pipeline as shipped uses no such path, evidenced by every request the stub recorded in BOTH arms having a path under /v1/ — and records the exception as an honest limit for 15.1 (§9 limit 9 at plan:3080-3084 currently covers only the schema observer). Row -non-v1-404-recorded. Task 11.8's row 11.8-models-and-404 already pins the same behaviour live, so this is a second, independent sighting, not a rediscovery.

SG-7 — ADMISSION'S TWO CAPACITY 503s ARE ALSO STATUSES THE DIRECT PATH WOULD NOT HAVE RETURNED (admission.hpp:11-16, :53-59: queue_timeout and queue_overflow). llama-server queues internally; the router can refuse. RESOLUTION: G5 equivalence is claimed BY CONSTRUCTION, not by luck — the generated config's `admission.maxInflightPerModel` is derived from the same number as llama-server's `--parallel` (plan:2870-2874), and the pipeline's peak concurrency is bounded by `parallel.maxImplementers + parallel.maxReaders`, so the run is required to show ZERO refusals AND a recorded peak in-flight/queue depth strictly inside the configured caps (row -no-admission-refusal-by-construction). The residue — a deployment whose concurrency exceeds its slots CAN be refused where the direct path would have queued — is recorded as an honest limit, not asserted away.

SG-8 — 'THE SAME COMMIT SET' AND 'THE SAME DISPOSITIONS' CANNOT MEAN BYTE-EQUAL (shas, runIds, timestamps and temp paths differ between two runs by construction, router or no router). RESOLUTION: comparison is over a NORMALIZED digest with a CLOSED, DECLARED allowlist of permitted differences — runId, all wall-clock times and durations, git object shas and committer dates, absolute fixture/temp paths, port numbers, and exactly one semantic difference (the report's Metrics section + `metricsAvailable`). Everything not on that list is compared verbatim (row -permitted-difference-allowlist-closed), and the comparator must be PROVEN to discriminate by a mutation (row -comparator-discriminates). Without both, a normalizer that quietly elides too much turns this whole step green forever — the exact failure mode C-034 banked.

SG-9 — A STANDING SUITE TEST THAT NEEDS A C++ BINARY AND A REAL opencode. Leg B needs `opencode` and legs A/C need `.out/build/clang-relwdebinfo/llama-router`; scripts/test-conductor.sh rejects any skip (C-015). RESOLUTION: follow the committed 0.2 precedent exactly — skip-tag the suite ONLY on binary absence and add an unconditional guard test asserting the coupling and that on THIS machine the suite really ran (wire-contract.test.ts:43-56, :339, :879), so an artifact-less machine degrades honestly instead of passing vacuously (row -skip-coupling-guard). ALTERNATIVE if the orchestrator does not want the Node suite bound to a C++ build artifact: ship the driver as a script invoked by hand with an M8-recorded artifact, exactly like 11.8. The default chosen here is the standing test, because plan:2885 says 'assert' and §11 row 9 says the equivalence step 'passes'.

SG-11 — A DELIBERATE DIVERGENCE FROM THE SIBLING 12.1-core SPEC, FLAGGED RATHER THAN BURIED. docs/build/specs/task-12.1.assertions.json (promoted concurrently with this file) carries its own row `12.1-g5-equivalence`, which agrees with LEG A row-for-row and with the sanctioned metrics/`metricsPartial` difference, but then records the no-traffic problem as a LIMIT: 'this proves the process is invariant to router presence for everything the harness controls — the model-traffic leg is 11.8's recorded failsoft equivalence and 13.2's live smoke, and this row must not be described as covering it'. THIS SPEC GOES FURTHER by adding LEG B, and the difference is deliberate: leg B does not add a MODEL (11.8 and 13.2 keep that dimension), it adds real PROVIDER TRAFFIC through the real router, using two already-committed fixtures (real `opencode serve` + stub-llm-server.ts). The reasoning is that 11.8's equivalence probe is ONE hand-issued curl pair recorded by a human, and 13.2 is a manual smoke — neither is a scripted, re-runnable assertion, so without leg B the ONLY automated evidence that the router does not break requests would be a comparison of two runs that sent it none. Leg B costs one extra opencode spawn per arm and reuses a vehicle that already runs in the suite. IF THE ORCHESTRATOR PREFERS THE SIBLING'S NARROWER SCOPE, drop rows -traffic-leg-router-actually-in-path, -status-equivalence-per-request, -schema-tagged-never-rejected, -stream-relay-equivalent and -no-admission-refusal-by-construction as a block and record the removal as an honest limit; do NOT keep them in weakened form, because a traffic leg that does not verify the ledger accounted for the traffic is exactly the vacuous test this gap exists to prevent.

SG-10 — WHICH SCENARIOS, AND HOW MANY TIMES? plan:2884 says 'the scripted e2e' without naming scenarios. RESOLUTION: ALL FIVE of 13.1's scenarios in both arms, including scenario 5's SECOND run in the same fixture (the stale-red-exclusion leg), because scenario 5 is where a router-shaped difference would most plausibly leak — it is the only scenario whose outcome depends on state written by a previous run. Running a subset would leave the cheapest-to-break path untested.

assertions.text: The two arms are constructed from ONE shared setup and are proven to actually differ. Both arms use: the same fixture-repo seed (same initial commit content and sha-independent file set), the same canned fake-SDK program (one `makeFakeSdk` construction re-used per arm), the same `.conductor/config.json`, and the same scenario list. Arm R additionally starts the real binary `.out/build/clang-relwdebinfo/llama-router --config <generated> --schema router/tests/schemas/RouterConfig.schema.json` on an EPHEMERAL port (never 8080, never the §2.2 default 8088 — the user's own llama-server may hold those), and the test asserts `GET http://127.0.0.1:<routerPort>/conductor/health` returns 200 BEFORE the scenarios start and again AFTER they finish. Arm N spawns no such process and the test asserts a connection to that same port is REFUSED at both moments. Each arm's proof is recorded in the artifact with the raw curl/health output.

Arm R runs the router config that 12.1-core's pure generator PRODUCES (`generate_router_config` in scripts/conductor_wiring.py, pinned by rows 12.1-router-config-shape and 12.1-parallel-single-source), never a hand-written file: the test calls the generator with the same host/port/`parallel.maxReaders` inputs serve.py would use, writes its output to the arm's config path, and asserts (a) the generated `admission.maxInflightPerModel` equals the integer in the `--parallel <slots>` argument of the llama-server command the SAME generator emits for the same inputs (plan:2870-2874 — one number, two consumers, no drift), (b) the generated `schema.rejectOnMissing` is false (plan:1671-1672 'must stay false in the base build'), and (c) the file parses under the exported schema — i.e. the binary starts on it with exit code 0 rather than the C-041 exit-3 ConfigError path.

The session opencode configs the two arms run under differ in EXACTLY one key. Arm N's provider `options.baseURL` is the upstream origin `http://<upstreamHost>:<upstreamPort>/v1` (the serve.py:217 shape, `--no-router` leg); arm R's is `http://<routerHost>:<routerPort>/v1`. The test deep-compares the two config objects with that one path masked and asserts they are otherwise EQUAL — same model/small_model, same merged conductor fragment (agent set, `tools.task:false` per C-014, the opencode auto-update pin per C-012), same plugin path. A difference anywhere else is a failure of this row, because it would mean the arms differ in something other than the router.

LEG A, the plan's headline (plan:2885-2886 'the same terminal state'): for EACH of 13.1's five scenarios run in both arms, the final `runs/<runId>/run.json` agrees on `state`, on `stop.kind`, and on `stop.reasonDisplay` verbatim. Scenario 5 is included with BOTH of its runs (the stopping run and the following clean-first-validate run), and the second run's `excludedStaleRed` list is compared as a set. Any inequality is reported naming the scenario, the field, and both values.

LEG A (plan:2886 'the same item dispositions'): for each scenario the item id SET is identical across arms, and for each id the normalized disposition record is identical — `state`; `blocked` as {reason, stage, questionId-present}; `deferred` as {reason, decisionId-present}; the ordered list of `taint` entry kinds; every counter in `attempts` (green, reviewRounds, vetRounds, testRepairs, debugFixes, overridesUsed); and the SET of evidence kinds present on the item (red/green/validated). Evidence seq numbers, timestamps and ledger offsets are normalized away; WHICH kinds exist is not.

LEG A (plan:2886 'the same commit set'): the commits each arm's run created in its fixture repo (everything after the seed commit, read through adapter/gitio.ts) are compared as an ORDERED list of {subject, name-status entries sorted by path}. Same length, same subjects verbatim, same per-commit file lists and status letters. Shas, author/committer dates and the fixture's absolute path are normalized away. The row additionally re-asserts, in both arms, that every created commit is trailer-free (no Co-Authored-By, no Generated-with) and carries no body — a router that somehow reached the commit path would show up here first.

LEG A: `runs/<runId>/report.md` is compared across arms section by section and is IDENTICAL in every section except Metrics — Items/dispositions, Open questions (ids included), Decisions, Stale-red additions and Exclusions must all match verbatim after path/id/time normalization. The permitted difference is exactly: arm R's Metrics section renders the summary returned by the injected §7.2 thunk and its handler return carries `metricsAvailable: true`; arm N's renders the metrics-unavailable line with `metricsAvailable: false` (9.5b's committed-by-then behaviour), together with the §4.4 failover/`metricsPartial` flags the sibling row 12.1-g5-equivalence also sanctions. The test asserts BOTH halves — that the Metrics sections differ in the expected direction (so arm R's router was genuinely consulted) and that no other section differs at all.

The normalizer's allowlist is CLOSED, DECLARED IN THE TEST FILE, and asserted to be exactly: runId; wall-clock times and durations; git object shas and committer dates; absolute fixture/temp/worktree paths; port numbers; and the Metrics section plus `metricsAvailable` and the §4.4 failover/`metricsPartial` flags. The comparison operates on the full artifact set — run.json, queue.json, items/*.json, questions.jsonl, decisions.jsonl, the journal's ordered (component,event) sequence, report.md and the commit list — with the allowlisted fields masked and EVERY remaining field compared. A test asserts the allowlist constant is the one the comparator actually uses (one source of truth, not a comment), so widening it later is a visible edit rather than a silent drift.

ANTI-VACUITY (the C-033/C-034 lesson made into a row): the comparator is proven to fail when it should. With the two arms' artifact sets captured, the test mutates ONE field of arm R's captured set at a time — an item's final `state`; one commit subject; one commit's file list; the run's `stop.kind`; one open question id — and asserts the comparison FAILS for each, naming the differing path and both values. It then asserts the UNMUTATED pair compares equal. A comparator that cannot be made to fail is not evidence, and this row is the only thing standing between a normalized digest and a permanently green non-test.

LEG B exists because 13.1 is model-free (SG-1): a scripted opencode conversation (the committed wire-contract vehicle — real `opencode serve` against `startStubLlmServer`) is run once per arm, identical prompt and identical fixture. The test asserts (a) the stub recorded at least one POST whose path ends `/chat/completions` in EACH arm, (b) in arm R the router's metrics ledger gained exactly as many request lines as the stub recorded requests and `GET /conductor/metrics` reports `totalRequests` equal to that same count, and (c) in arm N the router's ledger is untouched (no router was running). Without (b) the arms would be indistinguishable and every equivalence row below would be about a router carrying nothing.

LEG B, the G5 property itself (plan:90-91): pairing the two arms' recorded requests in order, each pair has the SAME HTTP status, and arm R contains ZERO router-minted statuses — no 502 upstream-unreachable envelope (router.hpp:817-819) and no 503 carrying `"type":"unavailable_error"` with code `queue_timeout` or `queue_overflow` (admission.hpp:53-59). The stub's recorded request bodies are compared field-by-field across arms and are identical except for opencode-generated ids, confirming the router forwarded verbatim rather than parse-and-re-serialize (router.hpp:15-22). Any router-minted status in this leg is a G5 FAILURE and fails the step, not a difference to be normalized.

LEG B, the §4.4 hazard exactly as the plan states it (plan:657-660, 1663-1673): under the 1.18.15 wire drift (wire-notes: prompt-body `format:{json_schema}` does not exist), every request the plugin tags `X-Conductor-Schema: required` via inject.ts:220-233 carries NO `response_format` and NO grammar/json_schema body field — i.e. is precisely the `schemaMissing` case. The test asserts each such request through the router is PROXIED and answered with the upstream's own status (the stub's 2xx), NEVER a 400; the response body reaching opencode is byte-identical to arm N's for the same request; the ledger's `schemaMissing` count equals the number of tagged requests; and the generated config's `schema.rejectOnMissing` was false. This is the single sharpest G5 row available without a real model.

LEG B, streaming (Task 0.2's finding: opencode's provider POSTs `stream: true` and consumes SSE `chat.completion.chunk` events): the client-visible event sequence in arm R equals arm N's — same ordered `data:` payload objects modulo opencode/stub-generated ids, same terminating `data: [DONE]` framing — and arm R's chunks arrive INCREMENTALLY (the first chunk is observed strictly before the last is sent, i.e. the response is not one buffered blob at completion), proving 11.3's unbuffered relay under real opencode traffic. The conversation completes in both arms with the same final assistant text and the same tool-call loop shape.

LEG B, SG-7's resolution: the equivalence is not luck. The test records, from arm R's ledger, the maximum concurrently in-flight requests per model and the maximum queue depth observed, and asserts max-in-flight <= the generated `admission.maxInflightPerModel` and max-queue-depth < `admission.maxQueued`, with ZERO queue_timeout and ZERO queue_overflow lines. It additionally asserts the config's cap is >= the pipeline's own concurrency bound (`parallel.maxImplementers + parallel.maxReaders` from the arm's `.conductor/config.json`), so refusal is unreachable by arithmetic rather than by the run happening to be slow. The recorded numbers go in the artifact.

LEG C, the fail-soft direction (plan:87-93 'layer 2 dies => layer 1 still enforces everything'): a third pass runs the LEG A scenarios in arm R with the router SIGKILLed after the run has started and before the report is produced. Its normalized digest — terminal state, item dispositions, commit set, every report section except Metrics — is identical to arm N's. The report renders the metrics-unavailable line with `metricsAvailable:false`; no unhandled rejection or uncaught exception is raised; no item transition, taint, question or stop is attributable to the router's absence; and any journal records emitted stay inside the closed `router-client` vocabulary (request | response | failover | retry, journal-events.ts:54).

LEG C, alive-but-hostile (the case a plain kill does not cover): with a process listening on the router port that answers `/conductor/health` with 500 and `/conductor/metrics` with a non-JSON body — and, for the traffic leg, forwards normally — the LEG A digest is STILL identical to arm N's and the report still renders metrics-unavailable. This exercises the fetchMetricsSummary non-200 and body-parse-failure paths (router-client.ts:206-228) end-to-end rather than through their unit stubs, and proves a degraded router cannot change a run's outcome.

LEG C, the recovery half that 12.1-core owns and this step observes: after the kill in -router-killed-midrun-still-identical, the 12.1-core supervisor restarts llama-router (delays following its pure capped-exponential backoff function, reset on a healthy run), the restarted process answers `GET /conductor/health` with 200, and a subsequent scenario run in the SAME arm produces the digest arm N produced — with `metricsAvailable:true` again. The artifact records the observed restart delays and the pid change. This is the real fail-soft story for provider traffic, given SG-5.

HONESTY (SG-5, the anti-overclaim row): the artifact states in plain words, with the file:line evidence, that §4.4's provider-traffic failover is NOT proven by this step — `resolveBaseUrl`/`noteRouterFailure` have no production caller at HEAD, `fanout.ts` never references the router, and opencode's provider baseURL is fixed by the session config serve.py writes at :217 and read at session start, so the plugin cannot divert provider traffic mid-session. The step therefore claims only what it observed (fail-soft probes, unchanged outcomes, supervisor restart), makes NO 'the session failed over' claim anywhere, and the limitation is queued for Task 15.1's HONEST-LIMITS. A green 12.1-G5 must not be readable as a proven failover.

HONESTY (SG-6): the artifact records the ONE G5 exception this pass found in committed router code — router.hpp:85-89 proxies `/v1/.*` only and 404s everything else, so llama-server's own /health, /props, /slots and /completion ARE failed by the router — together with the narrower true statement the run proves: every request the stub recorded, in BOTH arms, across every leg, had a path under `/v1/`, so the shipped pipeline never uses a path the router refuses. The exception is queued for 15.1's HONEST-LIMITS (§9 limit 9 at plan:3080-3084 currently covers only the schema observer); NO widening of the proxy pattern is proposed or performed by this step.

SUITE DISCIPLINE (SG-9, following the committed 0.2 precedent at wire-contract.test.ts:43-56/:339/:879): the G5 suite is skip-tagged ONLY when a prerequisite BINARY is absent — the `opencode` binary for leg B, `.out/build/clang-relwdebinfo/llama-router` for arms R — and an UNCONDITIONAL guard test asserts that the skip flag is exactly coupled to that absence and that on this machine neither was absent, so the suite really ran. scripts/test-conductor.sh rejects any SKIP/TODO directive at any depth (C-015), so on the build machine a skip here is a loud failure rather than a vacuous pass.
